parsed.explanation: Traveller-facing evidence is mostly positive. Gender identity and expression are protected under the national human-rights act and hate-crime provisions (2017). One province has a published human-rights commission policy and case law, and most jurisdictions allow self-declaration for documents. The dossier documents no trans-specific border, screening or visitor facility rule, though it also says border rules are unsourced, so that is an open question rather than an exposure. The main negatives are climate and resident-facing: a rising organised anti-trans movement, two school and healthcare rollbacks with override clauses, rising police-reported hate crime that is not disaggregated by gender identity, and reported abuse of trans prisoners. The 39% survey figure covers all 2SLGBTQI+ respondents over five years, so it carries little weight as current trans-specific prevalence. Hospital ward placement for visitors is undocumented. Overall, a documented protective framework with working recourse in some provinces sits well above the national-line tier, tempered by rollbacks, rising hate crime and unresolved visitor-facing questions.
